text:
anya: quick heads-up — i've been running long streaming sessions with the tool-loop workload and we see steady heap growth over ~30-60m, repro on staging with loadgen at 1.5k tokens/session. not a spike, a slow climb.

mike: can you paste the pprof/heap snapshot?

anya: here are the relevant bits from pprof (shortened):

```
pprof heap 30s
Showing top 12 nodes
nbytes  cumulative  allocs  object
3.6GB  3.6GB       12   runtime.mSpan
1.2GB  4.8GB      235   github.com/redwood/kv.(*Page).PIN
640MB  5.44GB     1.1k  github.com/redwood/serving/streaming.(*Session).buf
224MB  5.66GB     4.3k  runtime.concatstring
... (rest omitted)
```

tara: that PIN line looks suspicious — pages being pinned and not unpinned after tool loop iterations? :eyes:

sanjay: i turned on KV_DEBUG and instrumented pin/unpin counts. pin_count steadily increases and never returns to baseline after ~20k tokens; unpin calls are far fewer.

joel: i quickly grepped the tool-call fast-path and found code like: 
```
if toolCalled {
  return resp // early-return without unpin on this path
}
```
looks like an early-exit missing a defer/unpin.

mike: confirmed locally — added a defer page.Unpin() on the fast-path and mem profile stabilizes. small reproduce: run stream-tool-loop --iterations 10000, before: heap +2.1GB, after patch: <100MB growth.

anya: rolling a canary build to staging with the unpin fix + adding pin_count telemetry.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/kv-unpin-fix -> staging :rocket:

tara: also seeing fragmentation in the slab allocator. quick histogram from run: 
```
heap histogram
512B: 5.2M objs
1K: 3.1M objs
4K: 120k objs
64K: 20k objs
```
small-slab churn could be magnifying retention.

sanjay: proposal: 1) add unit test that spins tool-loop with early-return patch, assert pin_count returns to baseline; 2) add periodic coalesce/compaction pass after N sessions; 3) telemetry for avg page residency and pin/unpin ratio.

anya: i'll draft the test and PR today. will also enable a short-lived compaction on canary to validate no perf regressions.

mike: what about batching heuristics interacting with this? could batching delay unpin?

joel: good call — batching holds refs longer while queued. let's add a histogram of time-from-pin-to-unpin in metrics so we can correlate with batch size.

anya: action items: open PR for unpin fix + test (anya), add pin/unpin time metric (mike), run canary (tara), file incident ticket (joel). target: canary tomorrow, prod next week if clean.

ci-bot: opened issue INF-3247 "kv-page pin leak during tool early-return" and linked PR 4021

anya: thanks everyone — big win if this holds. i'll post canary results in this thread. :thumbsup:
